title: Problem statement confirmation
question: IsNull records 'absent' only for RGs with 2+ documents, so a one-document RG without the path is under-selected. The rule is deliberate and documented (README.md:344); the defect is that one index has two meanings for IsNull. The index already holds root-$ presence, so present($) minus present(P) can fix it at query time. Is this the problem we solve?
decision: Problem statement confirmed: one-doc RG lacking P is under-selected by IsNull; current rule is deliberate and documented; root-$ presence allows a query-side fix.

title: Meaning of IsNull in one-document RGs
question: Should an absent key count as null in every RG, including RGs with one document and plain 1:1 indexes?

options.text: Uniform: absent counts as null in every RG. One meaning per index. 1:1 indexes change: IsNull now also selects RGs whose document lacks the key (more RGs, never fewer). README:344, CHANGELOG note and 2 tests change.

Gated: change only indexes that look aggregated (NumDocs > RGs with documents). 1:1 indexes keep old answers. Does not fully fix TCLR: an aggregated file where each RG got one document looks like a 1:1 index and still under-selects (research F14).
Three-state (Couchbase family): IsNull = explicit null only, new IsMissing operator for absent. TCLR switches to NE ∪ IsNull ∪ IsMissing. Also changes multi-doc RGs, where IsNull covers absent today.

rationale: Prior art (RESEARCH-NULL-SEMANTICS.md): most systems collapse absent into the default null check (MongoDB, ClickHouse, Iceberg/Delta, SQL extractors); three-state systems use separate operators and none mixes meanings by data shape. Snowflake shows strict-null default causes the reported bug class. A keeps a narrow explicit-null operator possible later.
decision: Uniform meaning: IsNull(P) selects every RG holding at least one document with explicit null for P OR without P, whatever the RG's document count. Applies to 1:1 indexes too. Follows the MongoDB/SQL-extractor 'absent counts as null' family. A strict explicit-null-only operator is not added now; it stays possible later as a separate addition.
note: User asked for prior-art research on absent vs null before answering (RESEARCH-NULL-SEMANTICS.md).

title: Where the fix lives and the wire format
question: Where does the fix live, and does the format version change?

options.text: Query side: IsNull = null ∪ AbsentRGs ∪ (present($) minus present(P)). No format change, no size cost. Old v10/v11 indexes give correct answers when read. Depends on the rule 'root $ is present for every document' (pinned by a new test).

Build side: builder widens AbsentRGs to one-document RGs, format goes to v12. Decode rejects v11 files, so every user must rebuild. One more bitmap per path; 1:1 indexes now carry an AggregateIndex. Golden files regenerate.
Both: build side v12 for new files plus the query-side derivation for old ones. Most code, two paths that compute the same thing.

rationale: The data is already in the index. A fixes old files on read, which meets the issue's 'old indexes must not stay under-selecting' rule with no forced rebuild. B forces a rebuild for every user to store a bitmap the reader can compute.
decision: Query-side fix: IsNull = NullRGBitmap ∪ AbsentRGs ∪ (present($) minus present(P)). No wire format change, Version stays 11. Old v10/v11 indexes give correct answers when read. Builder and AbsentRGs layout unchanged. The 'root $ present for every committed document' rule gets a pinning test.

title: Release labeling of the behavior change
question: D1 changes documented IsNull answers for 1:1 indexes (README.md:344). How is the change labeled?

options.text: Patch v1.4.1, CHANGELOG 'Fixed' only. Understates the 1:1 change against a documented rule.
Minor v1.5.0, CHANGELOG 'Changed' (1:1 behavior, README rule) + 'Fixed' (#89). Matches PR #61 precedent (AbsentRGs shipped in minor v1.1.0).
Major v2.0.0. Go module path /v2, every importer rewrites imports, for a change that only adds RGs. Conflicts with the no-breaking-API constraint.

rationale: Not breaking under Evaluate's 'may contain' contract, but documented behavior changes, so a 'Changed' entry is honest. This task writes only the Unreleased CHANGELOG entry; the release cut stays a separate chore(release) commit.
decision: Minor release signal. CHANGELOG Unreleased gets a 'Changed' entry (1:1 IsNull behavior, replaces README rule) and a 'Fixed' entry (#89). Release cut is a separate chore(release) commit, not part of this task.
